topics.topic_label: Global AI governance blocs (Xi delivers the WAIC opening address in person - a first since 2018 - calling for AI to be 'a symphony of international cooperation' rather than 'a solo performance by a single country'; 29 countries signed WAICO into existence a day earlier, headquartered in Shanghai, the first standing international AI body China has convened rather than joined, landing 16 days before Brussels can fine GPAI providers)

Two-bloc AI governance (WAICO arrives as an explicit counterweight to Brussels as EU GPAI fines go live; GIRAI 2026 scores 135 countries on responsible-AI enforcement — 126 have policy but most stay non-binding, with unacceptable-risk government AI found in 35; Lawfare and the Obernolte–Trahan GAAIA draft debate a workable US federal AI law)

Two-bloc AI governance (Switzerland's Bundesrat Rösti pushes minimal global UN rules and ratifies the Council of Europe AI Convention rather than an EU-style act, as the WAICO/GIRAI two-bloc split hardens two weeks before Brussels can fine GPAI providers)
